what_its_for: Ubrogepant is used to treat migraine headaches with or without aura in adults. It helps relieve migraine pain and other symptoms like nausea and sensitivity to light and sound. It is NOT used to prevent migraines from happening — only to treat them once they start.
how_to_take: Take ubrogepant by mouth as a tablet, with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. You can take a second dose at least 2 hours after your first dose if your headache comes back or does not go away completely. Do not take more than 2 doses in any 24-hour period.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 50 mg taken by mouth as soon as a migraine begins. If needed, a second 50 mg dose may be taken at least 2 hours later. Your doctor may prescribe a 100 mg dose depending on your situation. Never take more than 200 mg total in one day. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
missed_dose: Ubrogepant is taken only when you have a migraine — it is not taken on a regular daily schedule, so there is no 'missed dose' in the usual sense. Simply take it when your migraine starts. If you forget to take it early in your migraine and your headache has already gotten very bad, it may be less effective, so try to take it as soon as possible after your migraine begins.
storage: Store ubrogepant at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it in a dry place away from moisture and heat. Keep the tablets in their original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use tablets past the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking ubrogepant with grapefruit or grapefruit juice, as it can increase the amount of medication in your blood and raise the risk of side effects. Avoid strong CYP3A4 inhibitors such as ketoconazole, itraconazole, clarithromycin, or ritonavir — tell your doctor if you take any of these, as your dose may need to be adjusted or the combination avoided. Avoid drinking alcohol while treating your migraine, as it can worsen headache and dizziness. Use caution when driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how this medication affects you, since it may cause drowsiness.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: a serious allergic reaction (hives, swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat, difficulty breathing); chest pain or tightness; sudden severe headache that feels different from your usual migraine; very severe dizziness or drowsiness; nausea or vomiting that is severe or unusual for you. Also contact your doctor if your migraines are happening more frequently, if the medication stops working, or if you feel you need to use it more than 10 days per month, as this could lead to medication-overuse headache.
when_it_works: Ubrogepant starts working within 1 to 2 hours for most people. Some people feel relief as early as 1 hour after taking it. It works best when taken at the first sign of a migraine, so do not wait until the pain becomes severe.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before using ubrogepant if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. It is not known if this medication is safe during pregnancy, and it may pass into breast milk. Kidney or liver problems: If you have severe kidney or liver disease, your doctor may recommend a lower dose (50 mg) and limit you to only one dose per migraine attack. Elderly patients: Ubrogepant can be used in older adults, but your doctor will monitor you closely. Children: Ubrogepant is approved for adults only and has not been studied in patients under 18 years of age.
